title: Weil-site and Galois cohomology comparisons
as_he_states: Prove the stated H/Ext calculation rules in the quasi-algebraic setting and compare Galois cohomology after passage to a perfect algebraic closure.
plausible_today: First define the manuscript site and coefficient category. For the modern ind-rational/pro-etale realization, use explicit proalgebraic/locally algebraic hypotheses and continuous Galois descent.
state_of_art: Suzuki2013 Theorem2.1.5 gives precise Ext comparisons; Suzuki2018 Proposition2.7.8 gives cohomological continuity and descent. Neither identifies every object of the handwritten quasi-scheme category.
why_open: The pages leave the site and comparison morphisms unfinished; the cited modern papers explain why larger sites and continuity are needed, rather than documenting a personal reason for abandonment.
worth: High priority as a source-to-modern-category dictionary; one run can match the generators and coverings without asserting an equivalence prematurely.

title: Continuity of the Neron realization
as_he_states: Interpret the functor through continuous maps or formal objects; the claim that it commutes with inductive limits is explicitly withdrawn.
plausible_today: Use finite Witt/Greenberg levels followed by the appropriate inverse limit, or prove continuity only for a restricted source system.
state_of_art: Suzuki2013 section2.1 and Suzuki2014 section3 set out realizations with finite-presentation/ind-rational control. The infinite-Witt counterexample in computations.md section2 independently verifies the reason for the withdrawal.
why_open: The author supplies the reason: the valuation/Witt construction does not commute with the direct limits in question.
worth: Worth developing as a precise finite-level correction of a withdrawn statement, not as a still-open blanket continuity conjecture.

title: Injectives and the first Neron spectral sequence
as_he_states: Check that N sends injectives to injectives; the attempted left-adjoint argument is cancelled.
plausible_today: It suffices that N sends injectives to Gamma_k-acyclic objects. An exact left adjoint would imply the stronger injective-preservation claim, but must actually be constructed.
state_of_art: Grothendieck1957 Theorem2.4.1 gives the exact composite-functor criterion. Suzuki2014 constructs the required derived realization with its own acyclicity arguments.
why_open: The missing acyclicity and cancelled adjunction are explicit on the page; no source states a further historical cause.
worth: High value for annotating the proof architecture; one run can identify the precise modern replacement for this gate.

title: First relative-Hom acyclicity gate
as_he_states: Verify the acyclicity assumed for the first relative-Hom spectral sequence.
plausible_today: Fix the uncertain first argument F/G and show that the selected resolution is acyclic for the outer relative-section functor.
state_of_art: The formal criterion is Grothendieck1957 Theorem2.4.1. Suzuki2013 Theorem2.1.5 gives related comparisons only for explicitly specified algebraic coefficient classes.
why_open: The text itself says the condition remains to be verified; no general theorem follows from left exactness alone.
worth: Worth a focused dictionary check after the category is fixed; no independent new theorem is currently identified.

title: Second relative-Hom acyclicity gate
as_he_states: Verify a second Hom/realization acyclicity condition before the comparison with global Ext.
plausible_today: Prove the derived adjunction or outer Gamma_k-acyclicity for the second composite independently of the first gate.
state_of_art: Grothendieck1957 Theorem2.4.1 supplies the conditional spectral sequence; Suzuki2013 Theorem2.1.5 and Suzuki2014 realization results give precise modern comparisons.
why_open: The second conditional is separately written; the source does not claim the first verification settles it.
worth: Worth retaining as a separate proof obligation so a future commentary does not lose one acyclicity hypothesis.

title: Self-duality of a Witt quotient
as_he_states: A marginal question accompanies proposed self-duality of a quotient W_n(K)/F^mW_n(K).
plausible_today: Specify quotient as a sheaf/pro-unipotent realization, the local residue pairing and F,V twists; an abstract group self-duality is not a substitute.
state_of_art: Milne2006 III sections5–6 gives height-one local duality; Suzuki2014 Theorem5.2.2.1 treats arbitrary finite-flat coefficients. These settle the finite-flat programme, but the exact handwritten Witt-quotient normalization was not matched.
why_open: The marginal question marks the missing application; no source found explains a later decision about this exact quotient.
worth: Moderate priority: a finite Witt-length residue calculation is a concrete next task once the notation is fixed.

title: Local Rosenlicht/class-field Ext comparison
as_he_states: Compare cohomology with Ext of J_K/k and the positive-degree expression involving J(K)/J(V).
plausible_today: Use the proalgebraic unit group and continuous abelianized Galois group, retaining residue-field and coefficient hypotheses.
state_of_art: Serre1961 section4 Theorem1 identifies the fundamental group of the proalgebraic units with the abelian Galois group for algebraically closed residue field; Suzuki2013 Theorem2.6.1 gives derived G_m/Z duality.
why_open: The particular all-groups positive-degree display is questioned and the manuscript does not define every comparison map.
worth: High historical value, but the next step is exact map comparison rather than a new existence theorem.

title: What is being perfected?
as_he_states: A circled parfait? appears beside k←V→K.
plausible_today: Keep perfect residue k separate from characteristic-p K, which need not be perfect; use the original K for flat mu_p and alpha_p cohomology.
state_of_art: Suzuki2014 works with a complete discretely valued field with perfect residue, not a perfect fraction field. Kummer and Frobenius give K*/K*^p and K/K^p, which disappear after perfecting K.
why_open: This is an explicit scope doubt; the calculations themselves show why indiscriminate perfection changes the problem.
worth: Essential reading correction to resolve with the scans, with a short mathematical countercheck already complete.

title: Acyclicity, bounds and base change for T
as_he_states: T0 should send injectives to Gamma_k-acyclic objects; the adjoining list proposes dimension2, dimension1 without Z-components and base-change compatibility.
plausible_today: Use coefficient-specific bounds for finite-flat groups, tori, lattices and abelian varieties in a defined geometrized realization.
state_of_art: Suzuki2014 Proposition3.4.3 gives exactly the different cohomological structures and degrees; Suzuki2013 Theorem2.1.5 provides comparison/continuity. No arbitrary-sheaf dimension bound follows.
why_open: Acyclicity is explicitly questioned; adjacent bounds are asserted without their necessary coefficient dictionary.
worth: High priority because it governs several later tables; a single run can produce a coefficient-by-coefficient translation.

title: Cartier, Serre and Pontryagin square
as_he_states: How is the lower duality square obtained?
plausible_today: Combine finite Cartier duality, Serre duality of the realized groups and derived finite-field Galois descent, with the resulting one-degree shift.
state_of_art: Suzuki2014 sections2.4 and10 construct the dualities/descent; Milne2006 I Theorem2.1 and III section0 give ordinary and geometric pairings. Exact commutativity with the handwritten N/T is not supplied by merely naming the three dualities.
why_open: The source asks for the morphism construction, not only an abstract isomorphism.
worth: A strong commentary task: specify every functor and natural transformation in one normalized diagram.

title: Local duality coefficient range and degrees
as_he_states: The local duality display excludes G_a constituents and contains changing degree1/degree2 conventions.
plausible_today: Separate finite-flat geometric local duality with one shift from ordinary local Tate duality after residue cohomology, and then treat wider affine coefficients by devissage with exact categories.
state_of_art: Suzuki2013 Theorem2.7.1 initially excludes a connected unipotent part; Suzuki2014 Theorem5.2.2.1 removes that restriction for finite-flat groups. Milne2006 I2.1 has ordinary local degree2. These exact scopes explain, but do not choose, uncertain manuscript exponents.
why_open: The manuscript is schematic and revises the coefficient restrictions; no reason for its unresolved indices is stated.
worth: High interest as a sign/degree normalization task; the next run should use the scans before changing any exponent.

title: The questioned local G_m and Z rows
as_he_states: Two question marks remain in the G_m/Z local duality rows, with character groups and H1(K,Q/Z) nearby.
plausible_today: Use the geometrized multiplicative group, derived characters and continuous Hom; distinguish it from the abstract group of k-points.
state_of_art: Suzuki2013 Theorem2.6.1 proves the precise local G_m/Z comparison; Suzuki2014 Proposition3.4.3 gives torus/lattice degree bounds. Ordinary finite-residue descent is addressed in its section10.
why_open: The page shifts among underlined Ext, double-underlined Ext and points without completing the comparison maps.
worth: Worth an exact row-by-row rewrite, especially to prevent arithmetic-unit conclusions from a geometric cohomology formula.

title: Component pairing and an alleged product splitting
as_he_states: Dual Neron component groups are paired in Q/Z; an upper product display accompanies a lower extension sequence.
plausible_today: For perfect residue fields the Grothendieck pairing is perfect. Retain the extension unless a splitting map is constructed; perfect pairings do not imply canonical product decompositions.
state_of_art: Suzuki2014 TheoremA proves perfectness over perfect residue fields by Galois descent, while its derived formulation retains component triangles. It notes failure over imperfect residue fields.
why_open: No splitting is proved on the page. The later paper gives a history of the perfectness problem, but no claim about this particular scratch-product symbol.
worth: High interest for a precise historical comparison; proving a new canonical splitting should not be a research direction without further evidence.

title: Biduality as completion
as_he_states: Interpret Delta squared and the compact/profinite-completion margin, including its uncertain degree.
plausible_today: Use Serre biduality on pro-unipotents and derived Tate-module completion on semiabelian parts, rather than a universal unshifted identity.
state_of_art: Suzuki2014 section2.4 identifies these different biduals and the uniquely divisible cone. Its exact category and shift conventions supply a verified comparison.
why_open: The manuscript leaves Delta versus0 and the completion notation unsettled; no later source decides the ink.
worth: High value as a categorical clarification; one run can match each graded piece and the component contribution.

title: How many internal Ext rows vanish?
as_he_states: The tables list0,B[n],0,0 and a torsion-limit analogue, then use a one-row Ext spectral sequence.
plausible_today: Internal fppf Hom(A,mu_n)=0, Ext1(A,mu_n)=B[n] and Ext2(A,mu_n)=0 follow from Barsotti--Weil and Ext2(A,G_m)=0. Higher degrees need separate theorems; global Ext inherits other cohomology rows.
state_of_art: RibeiroRosengarten2025 Theorem4.3 proves Ext2(A,G_m)=0 over arbitrary bases and explains a gap in an older argument. Its introduction gives a supersingular characteristic2 example with nonzero Ext3(A,G_m). Breen1975 supplies characteristic-dependent ranges.
why_open: The source gives a table without establishing the higher Ext input; the modern literature shows that category and degree restrictions are substantive.
worth: Highest priority for mathematical correction: write a finite-level derived truncation with all surviving rows before using any global collapse.

title: Divisibility of the discrete local H1 part
as_he_states: The discrete part of H1(K,A) is divisible, equivalently its dual is torsion-free.
plausible_today: In the geometrized complete-DVR/perfect-residue setting, finite-flat H2(K,A[n])=0 makes multiplication by n on H1(K,A) surjective; the discrete quotient inherits divisibility.
state_of_art: Suzuki2014 Proposition3.4.3(b,d), followed by the Kummer long exact sequence, proves this precise conclusion. It concerns H1 of an abelian variety, not G_m(S) for an arithmetic S.
why_open: The assertion is written without proof; no source documents why this local sheet was not completed.
worth: A useful short completed proof check, chiefly valuable for correcting the earlier project-context conflation.

title: Replace derived T(A) by a degree-zero object?
as_he_states: The final arrow asks whether H1(K,B[n]) equals Ext1 of the ordinary realized A with Z/n.
plausible_today: Specify a truncation triangle for T(A), then determine the obstruction terms from H1(K,A) and components before replacing it by H0.
state_of_art: Suzuki2014 TheoremA retains derived cohomology and biduality. The finite-flat theorem5.2.2.1 and component decomposition support comparisons in selected degrees, not the unqualified replacement.
why_open: The marginal question and incomplete item(iii) explicitly leave this simplification unproved.
worth: High interest and feasible in one focused run using an exact truncation triangle; no general replacement should be assumed.

title: The torsion limit and undefined Q,N
as_he_states: Pass to torsion limits, preserve B(K) tensor Q/Z, and interpret Q subset N in a cancelled scratch diagram.
plausible_today: The Kummer direct-limit short exact sequence is valid for abelian varieties over fields. There is no distinguished nonzero natural map B(K) to B(K) tensor Q/Z without choosing torsion parameters; Q and N need definitions.
state_of_art: Milne2006 I section3 and Suzuki2014 section3.4 use finite Kummer systems. Ext-continuity for the infinite coefficient sheaf is a separate issue; Suzuki2013 Theorem2.1.5 is only a comparison in its specified setting.
why_open: The source cancels one definition and leaves the subquotients unstable.
worth: Worth resolving only at the level of exact transition maps and truncations; the undefined subquotients are not an independently identified open theorem.

title: Local duality with the correct degree and dualizing object
as_he_states: The page asks whether a support-Ext expression equals D(M).
plausible_today: For regular local noetherian A of dimension r and finite M, use H_m^i(M)=Hom(Ext_A^{r-i}(M,A),H_m^r(A)); use dualizing complexes for broader rings.
state_of_art: SGA2 ExposeV Theorem2.1 proves the regular-local statement, following ExposeIV on injective dualizing modules. Matlis1958 gives the complete-local duality background.
why_open: The handwritten degree and support subscript are uncertain. The published theorem supplies the missing hypotheses, not a license to replace the ink.
worth: High historical value with a fully established mathematical endpoint; a commentary can give an explicit degree dictionary.

title: Support, thickening Ext and completion arrows
as_he_states: Express support Ext as a direct limit and identify the dual formal-completion arrows, the last target unfinished.
plausible_today: Keep X locally noetherian, F coherent, G quasi-coherent; use X noetherian for global Ext. Formal comparison also requires the exact finiteness and Mittag--Leffler/derived-limit conditions.
state_of_art: SGA2 VI Theorem2.3 proves the support-limit formula; IX Theorem2.1 gives formal functions under explicit hypotheses. Matlis1958 Theorem3.7 and the DVR calculation explain why completion appears.
why_open: The source leaves final arrows unlabelled. Dropping coherence is dangerous: root’s counterexample Hom(K,colim t^-nR/R) differs from colim Hom(K,t^-nR/R).
worth: High priority for linking these pages to cote43/161–162 and for keeping underived limits from replacing derived completion.

title: What are the C-groups and Weil objects?
as_he_states: Are the proposed k-groups defined like C-groups, and is this equivalent to the indicated Weil-functor/scheme definition?
plausible_today: Distinguish commutative fppf sheaves from representable or pro/ind-algebraic group objects; only assert an equivalence after specifying both full subcategories.
state_of_art: Suzuki2013 sections2.1–2.3 and Suzuki2018 section2 give precise geometric realizations. Their formalism does not identify an unspecified class of all manuscript objects.
why_open: The question is explicitly definitional; no later matching equivalence was found.
worth: Necessary foundational work, best bundled with MP-SA19-01 rather than treated as a separate existence conjecture.

title: Finite cohomological dimension for curve pushforward
as_he_states: Finite cohomological dimension is admitted for f_* before using spectral sequences.
plausible_today: For a smooth curve over perfect k and finite-flat coefficients, geometrized cohomology has degrees0,1,2; broader coefficients need their own bounds.
state_of_art: Suzuki2018 Theorem3.1.3 proves the finite-flat bound and duality on open curves. The ordinary topos f_* preserves injectives by exactness of inverse image, but a special premorphism needs extra checks.
why_open: The finite dimension is explicitly admitted; the page does not delimit all sheaves for which it is meant.
worth: A concise established-case annotation can settle the finite-flat use while preserving the broader question.

title: Construct the curve trace and its pairing
as_he_states: Define gamma:Rf_*S_sigma→sigma, then compose it with evaluation to obtain the fundamental comparison.
plausible_today: For G_m, use the Picard degree map as trace; finite-flat duality follows with compatible local valuation traces and compact-support pairings.
state_of_art: Suzuki2018 Propositions3.1.1–3.1.2 and Theorem3.1.3 give the trace and finite-flat duality; Propositions2.7.6–2.7.7 prove compatibility of localization pairings.
why_open: The source explicitly leaves the trace definition and an auxiliary morphism unfinished.
worth: Highest expository value: the next run can draw the actual evaluation/trace diagram and track its shift.

title: Curve duality beyond finite flat coefficients and modulo theta
as_he_states: State the finite/affine/no-abelian-component duality precisely and explain finite type modulo theta.

worth: Worth developing through a category glossary first; no present open problem should be assigned to an undefined quotient category.

title: Geometric reduction and Q/Z coefficient passage on curves
as_he_states: Reduce from finite etale sigma to the geometric case and Q/Z, while two formulas use opposite shifts of Rf_*G_m.
plausible_today: Use geometric finite-coefficient calculations and continuous descent, with Q/Z as a verified filtered colimit in the selected site; fix one derived-degree convention.
state_of_art: Stacks03RN computes finite prime-to-p cohomology; Stacks0A3J gives the p-primary input; SGA1 IX5.8 supplies the Jacobian character comparison. Suzuki2018 supplies the realization and trace.

title: Full p-torsion, etale realization and the paired F,V operators
as_he_states: Interpret the pi1(C) modulo p equals J[p] line and the duality of Frobenius kernels/cokernels, including maximal alpha_p subgroup and quotient.
plausible_today: Keep the finite group scheme J[p] separate from etale points; use Cartier duality with Frobenius twists and Oda’s contravariant Dieudonne module, then state the actual annihilator maps.
state_of_art: Oda1969 Cor1.3, Def3.5, Prop3.13, Thm3.19 and Cor5.11 give exact duality/operator data. The full-group-scheme pi1 reading is refuted by the supersingular elliptic example. A particular restricted-Lie p-operation still needs its own comparison.
why_open: Several glyphs and realization conventions are missing or uncertain; the text itself invokes autoduality rather than constructing the maps.
worth: High priority and well suited to one precise F,V diagram; avoid treating filtered de Rham data alone as the entire restricted-Lie identification.

title: Idelic and adelic complexes behind the table
as_he_states: Recover the table through multiplication by n on an idelic complex and Frobenius on an adelic one.
plausible_today: Specify complexes, residue/degree maps and compatible Kummer, Artin--Schreier and Frobenius triangles, then compare with the modern trace construction.
state_of_art: Serre1961 section5 provides generalized-Jacobian/idèle reciprocity; ArtinMilne1976 proves finite-flat curve duality through height-one methods; Suzuki2018 section3.1 gives compatible global/local traces.
why_open: Only the route and operator names are written; no exact chain map is supplied.
worth: A good bounded research task: work out one height-one coefficient and one prime-to-p coefficient before seeking a uniform complex.

title: Point-supported Ext and purity
as_he_states: Prove the point-supported Ext comparison with a two-degree shift.
plausible_today: For a codimension-one regular closed immersion and prime-to-p constructible torsion, use purity with the Tate twist. Wild flat groups need a different local statement.
state_of_art: SGA2 XIV2.3 records the codimension-one mu_n[2] dualizing normalization with SGA5 locators; Suzuki2018 section3.1 and its local terms provide finite-flat curve duality.
why_open: The page announces this as a proof obligation and later restricts n.
worth: Worth an exact normalization check with the source image; the established prime-to-p theorem is the correct first comparison.

title: Henselization and completion comparison
as_he_states: It is probably true that the support calculation may be made on the henselization.
plausible_today: For smooth or finite-flat groups, use cohomological approximation from henselization to completion; strict henselization and ordinary henselization have different residue Galois terms.
state_of_art: Suzuki2018 Proposition2.6.2 proves the needed approximation for these classes; Remark2.7.9 exhibits failure of a completion-based support comparison for arbitrary fppf sheaves.
why_open: The local wording is tentative and revised, with coefficient scope not fixed.
worth: A valuable completed-case annotation; the remaining work is identifying the exact manuscript neighborhood and coefficient class.

title: Extension by zero and the prime-to-p narrowing
as_he_states: Verify the extension-by-zero Ext comparison and an easy mu_n calculation; arbitrary n is cancelled in favor of n prime to p.
plausible_today: Use the exact open/closed sequence in the ordinary etale site. For the special flat realization use the proved localization triangles and do not restore the cancelled arbitrary-n scope.
state_of_art: SGA2 I gives support/excision; Suzuki2018 Propositions2.7.4–2.7.7 gives compatible flat-realization triangles. Stacks03PK distinguishes all-n fppf Kummer from invertible-n etale Kummer.
why_open: The author himself narrows the coefficient range; the reason is not explicitly stated beyond the promised calculation.
worth: High value for preserving a genuine withdrawal and for separating Kummer exactness from purity.

title: Compatibility of local and global duality triangles
as_he_states: Show the duality maps commute with the localization triangle and make the last vertical comparison an isomorphism.
plausible_today: Use a morphism of distinguished triangles with fixed cohomological shifts, retaining the quotient H1(K,N)/im H1(O_K,N) at the boundary.
state_of_art: Suzuki2014 Proposition5.2.2.2 and Suzuki2018 Propositions2.7.6–2.7.7 establish the compatibility. Suzuki2014 Proposition3.4.6 identifies the support term precisely.
why_open: The diagrams retain question marks and revised indices; the page does not prove the compatibility.
worth: High priority as the place where local and curve programmes meet; a modern commutative diagram can guide, but cannot replace, the ink check.

title: The final unshifted support/open box
as_he_states: Is boundary-supported cohomology of extension by zero unshiftedly isomorphic to cohomology on the open?
plausible_today: In the ordinary etale interpretation the box is false. The conditional shifted formula follows from localization when adjacent ambient groups vanish; the manuscript’s exotic relative notation needs definition.
state_of_art: SGA2 I Theorem2.8 gives the exact sequence. For X=P1,U=A1,Y=infinity,G=Z/l, H0_Y(j!G)=0 while H0(U,G)=Z/l. Suzuki2018 Remark2.7.9 supplies an additional warning for arbitrary fppf sheaves.
why_open: The author puts both a question mark and three further question marks after the box; the earlier margin already gives m+1.
worth: Resolve as a correction/reading task rather than develop the false ordinary formulation.

title: Multiplicity semicontinuity without assumed flatness
as_he_states: Can total geometric fibre multiplicity be upper semicontinuous under properness, universal openness and an S1 fibre, without assuming generic-fibre-point flatness?
plausible_today: The flat theorem is precise and established. The stronger universally-open extension must retain full support and embedded-prime conditions; the inequality-to-flatness sentence is a separate false assertion.
state_of_art: EGAIV3 Theorem12.2.1(xi), Lemma12.2.1.4 and Corollary12.2.2(iii) prove the flat case. Remark12.2.3(vi), pp182–183, explicitly repeats the remaining question. Exact EGA-number/associated-prime searches found no later resolution.
why_open: The published text identifies the unresolved associated-prime input. No claim is made that nonfinding in this search proves present openness.
worth: High interest for one backward-citation run because an exact published open question survives; first determine its later fate before attempting a proof.

title: Associated primes after quotienting by a parameter
as_he_states: With full support and a one-dimensional component, prove m belongs to Ass(M/tM); the avoided primes are uncertain.
plausible_today: If t avoids Ass(M), it is regular and depth gives the conclusion. EGA’s stronger question merely avoids minimal primes and expressly permits t-torsion.
state_of_art: EGAIV3 Remark12.2.3(vi) prints the stronger formulation. The regular-element case is independently proved in computations.md section19; the exact no-regularity fate was not located.
why_open: The precise difference between minimal and associated primes explains why a seemingly elementary reading can hide the published unresolved input.
worth: High interest, but the first step is an ink comparison and a citation search for the exact EGA question, not assuming the easy case answers it.

title: Missing equidimensionality hypotheses in a cancelled draft
as_he_states: Are the equidimensionality conditions in1.1(ii) and the equality condition in2.6 essential? A heading announces continuity of Cohen--Macaulay conditions.
plausible_today: For a proper finitely presented morphism and flat finitely presented module, the Cohen--Macaulay fibre locus is open. The missing preceding statements are needed to formulate their proposed generalization.
state_of_art: EGAIV3 Theorem12.2.1(vii) and local12.1.1(vi) give precise openness; section12.2.3 supplies counterexamples to removing neighboring hypotheses. No unique identification of1.1(ii),2.6 was found.
why_open: The whole remark is cancelled and its antecedents are absent, so the exact question cannot be recovered from a general theorem title.
worth: Documentary recovery has priority; mathematical development should wait for the missing typescript context.

title: Atiyah intrinsic join versus diagonal
as_he_states: The reused author supposes that Df and the diagonal-induced map have the same stable homotopy type.
plausible_today: Compare the two stable Thom maps with the exact bundle identifications gamma=−alpha−tau and delta=−beta−tau; equality of cross-section obstructions is weaker than equality of maps.
state_of_art: Atiyah1961 p309 contains the same conjectural wording. James/Atiyah/Adams–Walker/Sigrist–Suter backward searches found numerical cross-section results but no exact resolution of this map comparison.
why_open: This is Atiyah’s published question on reused paper, not a Grothendieck conjecture. No source found explains its later fate.
worth: Moderate priority outside the Jacobian dossier: a separate stable-homotopy literature task is warranted before treating it as currently open.

title: The deferred James numbers and real stable range
as_he_states: Determine q_k through J(X); the real theorem expressly says it makes no assertion for n<2k.
plausible_today: Use the established real, complex and quaternionic section classifications, while preserving the narrower scope of the reused Atiyah theorem.
state_of_art: Atiyah1961 Theorem6.5 gives the divisibility criterion in its stated range. AdamsWalker1965 primary extract states complete solution in the complex case; SigristSuter1973 main theorem and Theorem2.6 give the quaternionic numbers and explicitly identify q_k through Atiyah6.5.
why_open: The typed source promises future work; later primary texts show the numerical programme was pursued. This does not imply resolution of MP-SA19-36.
worth: Low priority for new research, useful for an accurate historical annotation and numerical-range check.

title: Incomplete property list and Euler-characteristic qualifications
as_he_states: The cancelled algebra draft leaves P blank and possibly instructs a proof for some properties; the Euler page has an uncertain doubt-word and a marginal strict inequality.
plausible_today: Use precise regular/depth/Cohen--Macaulay ascent results individually. The Euler leading coefficient is nonnegative without a nonzero hypothesis; the zero sheaf rules out an unconditional strict inequality.
state_of_art: Stacks00OG/00OO/0338 prove dimension, polynomial regularity and flat depth formulas; EGAIII1 Theorem2.5.3 gives the all-integer Euler polynomial and eventual section length. No source supplies the manuscript’s blank P list.
why_open: The omitted property list and uncertain doubt-word are documentary limitations, not evidence for an unspecified open theorem.
worth: A short reading-and-hypothesis task is worthwhile; no research direction should be built from the unfilled universal property placeholder.

title: Editorial questions and reused-sheet publication status
as_he_states: The cancelled outline asks about moving material to Chapter0 and carries Bott September1963?; a reused bibliography says to appear.
plausible_today: These are archival/editorial questions. Keep the local dates attached to their faces and identify the reused Atiyah text without dating adjacent handwritten duality pages.
state_of_art: Atiyah1961 pp308–310 matches the theorem sequence, final conjecture, references and institutional ending; receipt15March1960 and publication1961 date the printed work, not reuse of these sheets. EGAIII1/IV3 give precise mathematical matches without proving a folio chronology.
